newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan firm raided in insider trading probe - sources.
newsitem.headline: Japan firm raided in insider trading probe - sources.

text.p: Japan's securities watchdog on Wednesday began investigating whether a senior executive of Vitec Co Ltd had been involved in insider trading, sources close to the governmental body said.

Officials of the Securities and Exchange Surveillance Commission (SESC) raided the headquarters of the semiconductor trading firm and other locations including the home of the executive, the sources said.

The probe concerns suspicions that the executive bought 100,000 shares from the market in audio-visual equipment maker Shintom Co Ltd prior to the announcement in July 1994 of Shintom's third-party allocation of shares and establishment of a joint venture with two other companies, they said.
Vitec supplies Shintom with parts for its products.
The commission will consider whether to ask prosecutors to bring charges against the executive after reviewing the findings of its investigation, the sources said.
Vitec officials were not immediately available for comment.
Shintom officials also said spokesmen who would be able to comment on the investigation were not immediately available.
Shares in Vitec fell 130 yen to 1,010 yen on the over-the-counter market in Tokyo afternoon trading, depressed by the reports on the case. The yen was trading at around 112 yen to the dollar.
An SESC official, asked about a report of the investigation carried by Japan's NHK public television, said the commission could not comment.
